title: Uncle's Chicago visits and King Oliver's band
summary: The youngest brother's life, a 1933 trip to Chicago to see him, and the King Oliver band he worked with.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Alto, yeah. Is there anything else about your uncle? He was younger than your father, wasn't he?
Yes, he was the youngest brother.
Yeah, Peter was the oldest and my father in between.
Andre was the youngest. You mentioned that you had been up to Chicago once and saw your uncle there?

Well, yes. During the, it was the First World War. He passed through here. He had to go to the dentist and save his teeth. Fixed. And he went to Chicago and I didn't see him for quite a while. He came down here on the excursion and then he went back. And the next time I saw him, I went up on a boat with Sidney Desvane.
And I passed through there and saw him. That was in 1933. 1933. But when I finished high school, he gave me vacation up there. I started when I was 23.
Do you remember who he was working with in Chicago at that time?
Louis Armstrong, Baby Dodds, Lil, and I think they had a Jackson on the banjo.
